questions.questionText: Which reversible, 8-pin proprietary connector did Apple use on iPhones from the iPhone 5 through the iPhone 14?

explanation.correct: Lightning is Apple's reversible 8-pin connector, introduced in 2012 to replace the older 30-pin dock connector.
explanation.incorrect: Micro-USB and Mini-USB are non-reversible USB connectors used mainly by non-Apple devices, and the 30-pin dock connector is the older, larger Apple port that Lightning replaced.
explanation.examTip: Apple + reversible + 8 pins = Lightning.

metadata.examObjective: 220-1101 1.3 Set up and configure accessories and ports of mobile devices

questions.questionText: Which connector is reversible, supports USB Power Delivery, and has replaced micro-USB as the standard port on most current Android phones?

explanation.correct: USB-C is a small, reversible connector that supports data, video (alternate modes), and high-wattage charging through USB Power Delivery.
explanation.incorrect: Micro-USB and Mini-USB are older, non-reversible connectors, and USB Type-A is a larger rectangular host-side connector not used on phones.
explanation.examTip: If a port can be plugged in either way up and carries power and video, think USB-C.

metadata.examObjective: 220-1101 1.3 Set up and configure accessories and ports of mobile devices

questions.questionText: A technician notices a lightning-bolt icon next to a USB-C port on a laptop. What does the icon indicate?

options.text: The port only accepts Apple Lightning accessories
The port supports Thunderbolt (up to 40 Gbps with Thunderbolt 3 or 4)
The port is a proprietary docking connector for a single vendor
The port provides charging only and no data

explanation.correct: Thunderbolt 3 and 4 use the USB-C connector and can carry PCIe data, DisplayPort video, and power over a single cable at up to 40 Gbps.
explanation.incorrect: The Thunderbolt bolt icon is unrelated to Apple's Lightning connector, the port also carries data, and Thunderbolt over USB-C is an open standard rather than a single-vendor dock port.
explanation.examTip: A bolt icon on a USB-C port means Thunderbolt, not Apple Lightning.

metadata.examObjective: 220-1101 1.3 Set up and configure accessories and ports of mobile devices

questions.questionText: Select ALL connector types commonly used to charge or sync data with modern mobile phones and tablets.

explanation.correct: USB-C, Lightning, and micro-USB are all used for charging and data on phones and tablets, depending on the manufacturer and age of the device.
explanation.incorrect: DB-9 is a legacy serial connector and PS/2 is a legacy keyboard and mouse connector; neither is used on mobile devices.
explanation.examTip: Know the three mobile ports: USB-C, Lightning, and micro-USB (legacy).

metadata.examObjective: 220-1101 1.3 Set up and configure accessories and ports of mobile devices

questions.questionText: Match each device to the charging and data connector it uses.

dropdowns.prompt: iPhone 14
Google Pixel 8
Samsung Galaxy S5 (2014)

explanation.correct: The iPhone 14 uses Lightning, current Android phones such as the Pixel 8 use USB-C, and older Android phones such as the Galaxy S5 use micro-USB.
explanation.incorrect: Each wrong choice belongs to a different generation or manufacturer; for example, Apple did not use micro-USB, and USB-C was not yet common in 2014.
explanation.examTip: Date and brand the device: older Android = micro-USB, newer Android = USB-C, iPhone before 15 = Lightning.

metadata.examObjective: 220-1101 1.3 Set up and configure accessories and ports of mobile devices

questions.questionText: Drag each connector into the category that best describes it.

explanation.correct: Lightning and the 30-pin dock are Apple proprietary; micro-USB and mini-USB are older non-reversible USB connectors; USB-C and Thunderbolt 3 share the reversible USB-C connector.
explanation.incorrect: Thunderbolt 3 is not proprietary to Apple and does not use a Lightning-style connector; it uses the USB-C shape.
explanation.examTip: Thunderbolt 3 and 4 use USB-C connectors, but not every USB-C port supports Thunderbolt.

metadata.examObjective: 220-1101 1.3 Set up and configure accessories and ports of mobile devices

questions.questionText: Answer Yes if the statement is true, or No if it is false.

statements.text: The Lightning connector can be inserted in either orientation.
The micro-USB connector is reversible.
USB-C can carry both power and data.
Mini-USB is the standard port on current smartphones.

explanation.correct: Lightning and USB-C are reversible and USB-C carries power and data. Micro-USB is not reversible, and mini-USB is an obsolete connector.
explanation.incorrect: Micro-USB has a distinct top and bottom, and mini-USB is found on very old devices such as older cameras and MP3 players.
explanation.examTip: Reversible = Lightning and USB-C only.

metadata.examObjective: 220-1101 1.3 Set up and configure accessories and ports of mobile devices

questions.scenarioText: A salesperson uses an iPad Pro with a USB-C port and must present on a conference room monitor that has only an HDMI input. Wireless casting is not available in the room.
questions.questionText: Which accessory is MOST appropriate for this requirement?

options.text: A USB-C to HDMI adapter that supports DisplayPort Alternate Mode
A passive USB-C to USB-A adapter

explanation.correct: A USB-C iPad Pro can output video through DisplayPort Alternate Mode, so a USB-C to HDMI adapter or cable provides the wired connection to an HDMI-only monitor.
explanation.incorrect: A Lightning adapter does not fit a USB-C port, a USB-A to micro-USB cable carries no video, and a passive USB-C to USB-A adapter only changes the plug shape for data.
explanation.examTip: Video over USB-C requires DisplayPort Alt Mode (or Thunderbolt) support on the device.

metadata.examObjective: 220-1101 1.3 Set up and configure accessories and ports of mobile devices

questions.questionText: Answer Yes if the statement is true, or No if it is false.

statements.text: Capacitive touchscreens respond to the electrical conductivity of a finger.
Resistive touchscreens respond to physical pressure, so they can work with a gloved finger or stylus.
Most current smartphones use resistive touchscreens.
A lithium-ion battery should be fully drained before every recharge to preserve its capacity.

explanation.correct: Capacitive screens sense conductive touch, resistive screens sense pressure, and lithium-ion batteries have no memory effect so they do not need to be fully discharged.
explanation.incorrect: Most modern phones use capacitive screens, and fully draining a lithium-ion battery repeatedly shortens its lifespan.
explanation.examTip: Capacitive = conductive touch (multi-touch); resistive = pressure.

metadata.examObjective: 220-1101 1.2 Compare display components of mobile devices

questions.scenarioText: An employee reports that a company-issued smartphone was left in a taxi. The phone holds confidential data and is enrolled in the company's mobile device management (MDM) platform.
questions.questionText: What should the administrator do FIRST?

options.text: Order a replacement SIM card and take no other action
Use the MDM console to remotely lock the device and, if it cannot be recovered, remotely wipe it
Reset the employee's Active Directory password only
Wait 30 days to see whether the taxi company returns the device

explanation.correct: MDM allows an administrator to remotely lock, locate, and wipe a device so corporate data is protected even though the device is lost.
explanation.incorrect: Waiting leaves data exposed, resetting only a directory password does not protect data stored on the device, and a SIM replacement does nothing for the stored data.
explanation.examTip: Lost or stolen managed device = remote lock, locate, then remote wipe via MDM.

metadata.examObjective: 220-1101 1.4 Configure basic mobile-device network connectivity and application support

questions.questionText: Select the TWO statements that correctly describe NFC.

options.text: It transmits data over the cellular network
It typically works at ranges up to about 100 meters
It is commonly used for contactless payments
It works only over very short distances, typically a few centimeters
It requires a 6-digit PIN pairing every time it is used

explanation.correct: NFC is a very short-range wireless technology widely used for contactless payments, transit passes, and tap-to-pair features.
explanation.incorrect: A 100 m range is more typical of Bluetooth Class 1, NFC does not require PIN pairing for tapping, and NFC is not a cellular technology.
explanation.examTip: NFC = tap range (a few centimeters); Bluetooth = about 10 m for most devices.

metadata.examObjective: 220-1101 1.4 Configure basic mobile-device network connectivity and application support

questions.questionText: Answer Yes if the statement is true, or No if it is false.

statements.text: iOS is a closed-source operating system, while Android is based on the open-source AOSP.
By default, iOS apps are installed only from Apple's App Store.
Android devices cannot sideload apps under any circumstances.
Both iOS and Android devices can be managed with MDM software.

explanation.correct: iOS is closed source with a controlled app ecosystem, Android is built on open-source AOSP and permits sideloading, and both can be enrolled in MDM.
explanation.incorrect: Android allows installing apps from outside Google Play (sideloading) when the user permits it.
explanation.examTip: Open source = Android; closed source = iOS.

metadata.examObjective: 220-1101 1.4 Configure basic mobile-device network connectivity and application support

questions.questionText: Select ALL correct statements about handling swollen lithium-ion batteries in mobile devices.

options.text: Recycle the battery at an appropriate facility
Dispose of it in the regular office trash
Keep the battery away from extreme heat
Stop using the device and replace the swollen battery
Puncture the battery to release the pressure

explanation.correct: A swollen lithium-ion battery is a safety hazard that must be replaced, kept away from heat, and recycled through a proper facility.
explanation.incorrect: Puncturing a lithium-ion battery can cause fire and chemical exposure, and batteries must not go in the regular trash.
explanation.examTip: Swollen battery = stop using, replace, recycle; never puncture.

metadata.examObjective: 220-1101 1.1 Install and configure laptop hardware and components

questions.questionText: Select the cellular technology that matches each description.

dropdowns.prompt: Offers the highest peak speeds and lowest latency, including mmWave bands
Based on Long Term Evolution standards
Provides slower data service and is being phased out in many regions

explanation.correct: 5G provides the highest speeds and lowest latency, 4G LTE is based on Long Term Evolution, and 3G is the older, slower generation being retired.
explanation.incorrect: Each generation matches only one description based on speed, latency, and the technologies it uses.
explanation.examTip: Generations in order of speed: 3G < 4G LTE < 5G.

metadata.examObjective: 220-1101 1.4 Configure basic mobile-device network connectivity and application support

questions.questionText: Place the steps for pairing a Bluetooth accessory with a mobile device in the correct order.

orderItems.text: Enable Bluetooth on the mobile device
Enable pairing mode on the accessory
Enter the PIN code if prompted
Locate the accessory in the list of available devices and select it

explanation.correct: The standard sequence is enable Bluetooth, put the accessory in pairing mode, select it, enter a PIN if requested, and then test.
explanation.incorrect: Selecting a device before it is discoverable, or testing before pairing completes, will fail.
explanation.examTip: CompTIA Bluetooth steps: enable, pairing mode, find, PIN, test.

metadata.examObjective: 220-1101 1.4 Configure basic mobile-device network connectivity and application support

questions.questionText: At which OSI layer does a router make forwarding decisions based on IP addresses?

explanation.correct: Routers operate at Layer 3 and forward packets between networks using IP addresses.
explanation.incorrect: Layer 1 moves raw bits, Layer 2 uses MAC addresses (switches), and Layer 4 uses ports (TCP/UDP).
explanation.examTip: IP address = Layer 3; MAC address = Layer 2; port = Layer 4.

metadata.examObjective: 220-1101 2.2 Compare common networking hardware

questions.questionText: Which network device forwards frames to a specific port based on destination MAC addresses?

explanation.correct: A switch builds a MAC address table and forwards frames only out the port where the destination device is located.
explanation.incorrect: A hub and a repeater send signals out all ports without examining MAC addresses, and a modem modulates signals for a WAN link.
explanation.examTip: Switch = Layer 2 and MAC addresses.

metadata.examObjective: 220-1101 2.2 Compare common networking hardware

questions.questionText: Select ALL protocols that encrypt their traffic.

explanation.correct: HTTPS, SSH, and SFTP all encrypt data in transit.
explanation.incorrect: Telnet and FTP send credentials and data in clear text.
explanation.examTip: Replace Telnet with SSH and FTP with SFTP or FTPS.

metadata.examObjective: 220-1101 2.1 Compare TCP and UDP ports, protocols, and their purposes

questions.questionText: A workstation shows an IP address of 169.254.37.12 and cannot reach the Internet. What does this MOST likely indicate?

options.text: The DNS server returned an incorrect record
The default gateway has been configured twice
The workstation could not reach a DHCP server and assigned itself an APIPA address
The workstation has a valid static public IP address

explanation.correct: Addresses in 169.254.0.0/16 are APIPA addresses that Windows self-assigns when DHCP is unavailable.
explanation.incorrect: APIPA addresses are not public, are not the result of DNS problems, and are not caused by duplicate gateway settings.
explanation.examTip: 169.254.x.x means DHCP failed.

metadata.examObjective: 220-1101 2.6 Compare common network configuration concepts

questions.questionText: Answer Yes if the statement is true, or No if it is false.

statements.text: A /24 subnet mask is 255.255.255.0.
A /26 subnet mask is 255.255.255.192.
192.168.1.255 with a /24 mask is a valid host address.
169.254.x.x addresses are routable on the public Internet.

explanation.correct: A /24 is 255.255.255.0 and a /26 is 255.255.255.192. In a /24, .255 is the broadcast address, and APIPA addresses are link-local only.
explanation.incorrect: The broadcast address cannot be assigned to a host and link-local addresses are not routed.
explanation.examTip: First address = network ID; last = broadcast; neither is a host address.

metadata.examObjective: 220-1101 2.6 Compare common network configuration concepts

questions.scenarioText: A user can browse to http://203.0.113.10 but cannot open www.example.com. Other users on the same network have the same problem.
questions.questionText: Which tool should the technician use to verify DNS name resolution?

explanation.correct: Because the IP address works but the hostname does not, name resolution is suspect, and nslookup queries DNS servers directly.
explanation.incorrect: tracert shows the routing path, netstat shows connections, and ipconfig /release drops the DHCP lease without testing DNS.
explanation.examTip: IP works, name fails = DNS; use nslookup.

metadata.examObjective: 220-1101 2.8 Use networking tools

questions.questionText: Select the correct value for each subnetting question.

dropdowns.prompt: Subnet mask for /24
Usable host addresses in a /26 network
Usable host addresses in a /30 network

explanation.correct: A /24 mask is 255.255.255.0, a /26 has 64 total addresses with 62 usable, and a /30 has 4 total addresses with 2 usable.
explanation.incorrect: Usable hosts equal 2^n minus 2 (network and broadcast addresses).
explanation.examTip: Usable hosts = 2^(host bits) - 2.

metadata.examObjective: 220-1101 2.6 Compare common network configuration concepts

questions.questionText: Which wireless standard operates ONLY in the 5 GHz band?

explanation.correct: 802.11ac (Wi-Fi 5) operates only in the 5 GHz band.
explanation.incorrect: 802.11b and 802.11g use 2.4 GHz, and 802.11n can use both 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz.
explanation.examTip: ac = 5 GHz only; n = dual-band; b/g = 2.4 GHz.

metadata.examObjective: 220-1101 2.3 Compare protocols for wireless networking

questions.questionText: Select ALL wireless standards that can operate in the 5 GHz band.

explanation.correct: 802.11a, 802.11n, and 802.11ac can use 5 GHz.
explanation.incorrect: 802.11b and 802.11g operate only in 2.4 GHz.
explanation.examTip: Only a, n, ac, and ax use 5 GHz.

metadata.examObjective: 220-1101 2.3 Compare protocols for wireless networking

questions.questionText: Select the TWO best practices for securing a SOHO wireless router.

options.text: Keep the default SSID and password printed on the router
Use WPA3 (or WPA2 with AES) and a strong passphrase

explanation.correct: Disabling WPS removes a brute-forceable PIN weakness, and modern encryption with a strong passphrase protects the traffic.
explanation.incorrect: Default credentials and WEP are easily compromised.
explanation.examTip: Change defaults, disable WPS, and use WPA3/WPA2-AES.

metadata.examObjective: 220-1101 2.5 Install and configure basic wired/wireless SOHO networks

questions.questionText: Select ALL addresses that are within private IPv4 ranges (RFC 1918).

explanation.incorrect: 172.32.4.1 is outside the 172.16-172.31 range, and 169.254.1.1 is link-local APIPA space.
explanation.examTip: The 172 private range ends at 172.31.

metadata.examObjective: 220-1101 2.6 Compare common network configuration concepts

questions.questionText: Answer Yes if the statement is true, or No if it is false.

statements.text: IPv6 addresses are 128 bits long.
IPv6 relies on broadcast to reach all hosts.
::1 is the IPv6 loopback address.
IPv6 addresses are written in dotted-decimal notation.

explanation.correct: IPv6 uses 128-bit addresses written in hexadecimal, ::1 is loopback, and IPv6 replaces broadcast with multicast.
explanation.incorrect: Dotted-decimal is IPv4 notation, and IPv6 has no broadcast.
explanation.examTip: IPv4 = 32 bits dotted decimal; IPv6 = 128 bits hex.

metadata.examObjective: 220-1101 2.6 Compare common network configuration concepts

questions.questionText: Answer Yes if the statement is true, or No if it is false.

statements.text: 802.11ax devices that support Wi-Fi 6E can use the 6 GHz band.
WPA3-Personal replaces the pre-shared key handshake with SAE.
Disabling SSID broadcast is a strong security control.
The WPS PIN method is considered secure against brute-force attacks.

explanation.correct: Wi-Fi 6E extends 802.11ax into 6 GHz, and WPA3-Personal uses SAE. Hidden SSIDs are easily discovered and WPS PINs can be brute-forced.
explanation.incorrect: SSID hiding is obscurity, not security, and WPS PIN attacks are well known.
explanation.examTip: Hidden SSID and WPS are not real security controls.

metadata.examObjective: 220-1101 2.3 Compare protocols for wireless networking

questions.questionText: Select the tool that best fits each task.

dropdowns.prompt: Trace the path packets take to a remote host
Query DNS for the IP address of a hostname
Display active connections and listening ports
Show adapter IP address, mask, and default gateway

explanation.correct: tracert maps hops, nslookup queries DNS, netstat lists connections, and ipconfig displays adapter settings.
explanation.incorrect: ping only tests reachability and does not map paths, query DNS, or list connections.
explanation.examTip: Know the job of each command-line tool.

metadata.examObjective: 220-1101 2.8 Use networking tools

questions.questionText: Select the default port for each service.

dropdowns.prompt: SSH
SMTP
RDP
DNS

explanation.correct: SSH uses 22, SMTP uses 25, RDP uses 3389, and DNS uses 53.
explanation.incorrect: Port 23 is Telnet, which is not used by any of these services.
explanation.examTip: Memorize the common ports: 22, 23, 25, 53, 80, 443, 3389.

metadata.examObjective: 220-1101 2.1 Compare TCP and UDP ports, protocols, and their purposes

questions.questionText: Place the OSI layers in order from Layer 1 to Layer 7.

explanation.correct: The order from Layer 1 upward is Physical, Data Link, Network, Transport, Session, Presentation, Application.
explanation.incorrect: Session and Presentation are commonly swapped; Presentation sits above Session.
explanation.examTip: Mnemonic: Please Do Not Throw Sausage Pizza Away.

metadata.examObjective: 220-1101 2.2 Compare common networking hardware

questions.questionText: Place the four steps of the DHCP process in the correct order.

explanation.correct: DHCP follows Discover, Offer, Request, Acknowledge (DORA).
explanation.incorrect: The client requests only after it has received an offer.
explanation.examTip: DORA = Discover, Offer, Request, Acknowledge.

metadata.examObjective: 220-1101 2.6 Compare common network configuration concepts

questions.questionText: Drag each networking device to the OSI layer where it primarily operates.

explanation.correct: Hubs and repeaters work with electrical signals at Layer 1, switches and bridges use MAC addresses at Layer 2, and routers and Layer 3 switches use IP addresses at Layer 3.
explanation.incorrect: A Layer 3 switch routes by IP, so it does not belong with the pure Layer 2 devices.
explanation.examTip: IP-aware devices live at Layer 3.

metadata.examObjective: 220-1101 2.2 Compare common networking hardware

questions.scenarioText: In a dense apartment building, a technician sees many SSIDs overlapping on 2.4 GHz channels and the users report slow, unreliable Wi-Fi.
questions.questionText: Which action will MOST likely reduce the interference?

options.text: Set the access points to channel 3
Move the access points to the 5 GHz band
Enable WPS on every access point
Increase the transmit power on every access point

explanation.correct: The 5 GHz band has many more non-overlapping channels and less congestion than 2.4 GHz.
explanation.incorrect: More power increases interference, channel 3 overlaps with channels 1 and 6, and WPS has no effect on interference.
explanation.examTip: 2.4 GHz non-overlapping channels are 1, 6, and 11.

metadata.examObjective: 220-1101 2.5 Install and configure basic wired/wireless SOHO networks

questions.scenarioText: A user can ping the default gateway successfully but cannot reach any Internet sites. A tracert to 8.8.8.8 shows the first hop responding and every later hop timing out.
questions.questionText: Where is the problem MOST likely located?

options.text: Beyond the local gateway, on the ISP or WAN side

explanation.correct: If the gateway replies and later hops time out, the failure is beyond the local network.
explanation.incorrect: A bad NIC or cable would prevent reaching the gateway, and DNS is not involved when tracing by IP address.
explanation.examTip: Find the last responding hop to locate the break.

metadata.examObjective: 220-1101 2.8 Use networking tools

questions.questionText: Which motherboard form factor is the smallest of the following?

explanation.correct: Mini-ITX boards measure 170 mm x 170 mm, making them the smallest of the listed form factors.
explanation.incorrect: ATX (305 x 244 mm) and microATX (244 x 244 mm) are larger, and Extended ATX is larger still.
explanation.examTip: Size order: E-ATX > ATX > microATX > Mini-ITX.

metadata.examObjective: 220-1101 3.4 Install and configure motherboards, CPUs, and add-on cards

questions.questionText: Which memory module form factor is used in most laptops?

explanation.correct: SO-DIMMs are about half the length of desktop DIMMs and are used in laptops and small form factor systems.
explanation.incorrect: Full-size DIMMs are for desktops, and SIMMs and RIMMs are obsolete.
explanation.examTip: Laptop RAM = SO-DIMM.

metadata.examObjective: 220-1101 3.2 Compare different types of RAM

questions.questionText: An SSD is labeled M.2 2280. What does '2280' describe?

options.text: The drive has 2,280 GB of capacity
The drive uses 22 PCIe lanes and 80 pins
The module is 22 mm wide and 80 mm long
The drive was manufactured in week 22 of 2080

explanation.correct: M.2 size codes encode width and length in millimeters, so 2280 is 22 mm x 80 mm.
explanation.incorrect: The code is a physical size, not capacity, lane count, or date.
explanation.examTip: 2280 = 22 x 80 mm, the most common M.2 length.

metadata.examObjective: 220-1101 3.3 Install and configure storage devices (including RAID)

questions.scenarioText: A technician must replace a failed motherboard in an ATX mid-tower case. The only replacement available from stock is a microATX board.
questions.questionText: Will the microATX motherboard fit in the ATX case?

options.text: Yes, microATX boards use a subset of ATX mounting holes and fit ATX cases
Only if the case uses an SFX power supply
No, microATX boards require a dedicated microATX case
Only if an adapter bracket is purchased

explanation.correct: microATX boards were designed to be backward compatible with ATX cases by using a subset of the same standoff positions.
explanation.incorrect: No adapter or special power supply is needed, and ATX cases generally support smaller boards.
explanation.examTip: Smaller boards fit in larger cases; larger boards do not fit in smaller cases.

metadata.examObjective: 220-1101 3.4 Install and configure motherboards, CPUs, and add-on cards

questions.questionText: Which power supply form factor is designed for small form factor and Mini-ITX builds?

explanation.correct: SFX power supplies are physically smaller than standard ATX units and are used in compact cases.
explanation.incorrect: ATX is the standard desktop size, EPS is a CPU power connector type, and Molex is a legacy 4-pin connector.
explanation.examTip: SFX = small form factor power supply.

metadata.examObjective: 220-1101 3.5 Install the appropriate power supply

questions.questionText: Which RAID level provides mirroring using two drives?

explanation.correct: RAID 1 mirrors the same data to two drives so either drive can fail without data loss.
explanation.incorrect: RAID 0 stripes with no redundancy, RAID 5 uses parity across three or more drives, and RAID 6 uses double parity.
explanation.examTip: RAID 1 = mirroring.

metadata.examObjective: 220-1101 3.3 Install and configure storage devices (including RAID)

questions.scenarioText: A small business is building a database server with four identical drives. It needs strong write performance and the ability to survive a single drive failure without parity calculation overhead.
questions.questionText: Which RAID level should the technician choose?

explanation.correct: RAID 10 combines mirroring and striping, offering strong performance and fault tolerance without parity calculation overhead and needing at least four drives.
explanation.incorrect: RAID 0 has no fault tolerance, RAID 1 does not stripe, and RAID 5 uses parity that adds write overhead.
explanation.examTip: Four drives, speed, and redundancy without parity = RAID 10.

metadata.examObjective: 220-1101 3.3 Install and configure storage devices (including RAID)

questions.questionText: Which connector supplies main power from the power supply to an ATX motherboard?

explanation.correct: The 24-pin ATX connector is the main power connector for the motherboard.
explanation.incorrect: Molex and SATA power connectors feed drives, and the PCIe power connector feeds video cards.
explanation.examTip: 24-pin ATX = motherboard; 4+4 EPS = CPU.

metadata.examObjective: 220-1101 3.5 Install the appropriate power supply

questions.questionText: Toner on the printed page smears and rubs off easily. Which laser printer component is MOST likely failing?

explanation.correct: The fuser uses heat and pressure to bond toner to the paper, so smearing indicates it is not working properly.
explanation.incorrect: The drum, charging components, and pickup rollers cause different symptoms such as repeating marks, light prints, or paper jams.
explanation.examTip: Toner rubs off = fuser.

metadata.examObjective: 220-1101 5.6 Troubleshoot printer problems

questions.scenarioText: A technician installs an NVMe M.2 SSD into a laptop's M.2 slot. The drive is not detected in the BIOS, and the laptop manual says the slot supports SATA only.
questions.questionText: What is the MOST likely cause?

options.text: The OS needs a new keyboard driver
The SSD requires a RAID controller card
The boot order is set to network first
The M.2 slot supports only SATA-based M.2 drives, not NVMe

explanation.correct: M.2 is a form factor that can carry SATA or PCIe NVMe; if the slot supports only SATA, an NVMe drive will not be detected.
explanation.incorrect: Keyboard drivers and boot order do not affect device detection, and RAID is not required for a single drive.
explanation.examTip: Check M.2 slot support (SATA vs PCIe/NVMe) and key type (B-key vs M-key).

metadata.examObjective: 220-1101 3.4 Install and configure motherboards, CPUs, and add-on cards

questions.scenarioText: A technician installs two identical 8 GB DDR4 DIMMs in one blue slot and one black slot. The motherboard manual says dual-channel operation requires modules in the same-colored slots, and system information shows single-channel mode.
questions.questionText: What should the technician do to enable dual-channel mode?

options.text: Replace the DIMMs with DDR5 modules
Switch the BIOS to legacy mode
Move both DIMMs into matching-colored slots as indicated in the motherboard manual

explanation.correct: Dual-channel mode generally requires matched DIMMs installed in the specific slot pairs identified by the motherboard manual, often same-colored slots.
explanation.incorrect: DDR5 would be incompatible with a DDR4 board, an extra DIMM is unnecessary, and legacy mode does not affect memory channels.
explanation.examTip: Same-colored slots = a dual-channel pair on most boards.

metadata.examObjective: 220-1101 3.2 Compare different types of RAM

questions.questionText: Select ALL valid motherboard form factors.

explanation.correct: ATX, microATX, and Mini-ITX are motherboard form factors.
explanation.incorrect: SFX is a power supply form factor and NVMe is a storage protocol.
explanation.examTip: SFX is for power supplies, not motherboards.

metadata.examObjective: 220-1101 3.4 Install and configure motherboards, CPUs, and add-on cards

questions.questionText: Select ALL RAID levels that provide fault tolerance.

explanation.correct: RAID 1, 5, and 10 can survive at least one drive failure.
explanation.incorrect: RAID 0 and JBOD provide no redundancy.
explanation.examTip: RAID 0 = zero fault tolerance.

metadata.examObjective: 220-1101 3.3 Install and configure storage devices (including RAID)

questions.scenarioText: A desktop PC shuts down randomly when running demanding applications. The case is warm, and the fans have not been cleaned in years.
questions.questionText: Select the TWO most likely causes.

options.text: The keyboard layout is set incorrectly
A failed CPU fan or dried thermal paste

explanation.correct: Random shutdowns under load are a classic overheating symptom, caused by cooling failures such as a failed fan, dried thermal paste, or dust-clogged heatsinks.
explanation.incorrect: Keyboard layout, time zone, and network cable issues do not make a PC shut down under load.
explanation.examTip: Random shutdown under load = think thermal first.

metadata.examObjective: 220-1101 5.2 Troubleshoot problems related to motherboards, RAM, CPU, and power

questions.questionText: Select ALL devices normally powered by a SATA power connector.

explanation.correct: SATA drives and SATA optical drives use the 15-pin SATA power connector.
explanation.incorrect: CPUs use EPS/ATX 12V connectors and high-end GPUs use PCIe power connectors.
explanation.examTip: SATA power = storage drives and optical drives.

metadata.examObjective: 220-1101 3.1 Explain basic cable types and connectors

questions.questionText: Answer Yes if the statement is true, or No if it is false.

statements.text: An ATX motherboard fits in a case built only for microATX boards.
A Mini-ITX board can be mounted in an ATX case.
An SO-DIMM is physically smaller than a desktop DIMM.
A 3.5-inch hard drive fits in a 2.5-inch bay without an adapter.

explanation.correct: Smaller boards fit larger cases, SO-DIMMs are shorter than DIMMs, and 3.5-inch drives are too large for 2.5-inch bays.
explanation.incorrect: Larger boards cannot fit smaller cases.
explanation.examTip: Smaller form factors fit larger cases but not the reverse.

metadata.examObjective: 220-1101 3.4 Install and configure motherboards, CPUs, and add-on cards

questions.questionText: Answer Yes if the statement is true, or No if it is false.

statements.text: SSDs have no moving parts.
Hard drives generally have faster random access than SSDs.
NVMe SSDs communicate over PCIe.
SSDs should be defragmented regularly for best performance.

explanation.correct: SSDs have no moving parts and NVMe uses PCIe. Defragmenting SSDs is unnecessary and adds wear.
explanation.incorrect: HDDs have mechanical seek times, so random access is slower.
explanation.examTip: Do not defrag SSDs; TRIM and optimization handle them.

metadata.examObjective: 220-1101 3.3 Install and configure storage devices (including RAID)

questions.questionText: Answer Yes if the statement is true, or No if it is false.

statements.text: RAID 5 requires a minimum of three drives.
RAID 0 provides fault tolerance.
A two-drive RAID 1 array yields about 50 percent usable capacity.
RAID 10 requires a minimum of four drives.

explanation.correct: RAID 5 needs at least three drives, RAID 1 yields half the raw capacity, and RAID 10 needs four drives.
explanation.incorrect: RAID 0 stripes data and has no redundancy.
explanation.examTip: Min drives: RAID 0/1 = 2, RAID 5 = 3, RAID 10 = 4.

metadata.examObjective: 220-1101 3.3 Install and configure storage devices (including RAID)

questions.questionText: Answer Yes if the statement is true, or No if it is false.

statements.text: Impact printers can produce multipart carbon-copy forms.
Thermal printers use liquid ink cartridges.
Laser printers use heat and pressure to fuse toner to paper.
Inkjet printers can use thermal or piezoelectric methods to propel ink.

explanation.correct: Impact printers strike through multipart forms, lasers fuse toner, and inkjets use thermal or piezoelectric propulsion.
explanation.incorrect: Thermal printers use heat-sensitive paper or a thermal transfer ribbon, not liquid ink cartridges.
explanation.examTip: Thermal = receipts and labels; impact = multipart forms.

metadata.examObjective: 220-1101 3.6 Deploy and configure multifunction devices/printers

questions.questionText: Drag each storage device into the form factor or slot it uses.

explanation.correct: Laptop drives and many SATA SSDs use 2.5-inch bays, desktop and NAS hard drives use 3.5-inch bays, and NVMe and M.2 SATA SSDs use M.2 slots.
explanation.incorrect: M.2 drives are small modules and cannot be mounted in a drive bay without an adapter.
explanation.examTip: M.2 is a form factor; NVMe and SATA are interfaces.

metadata.examObjective: 220-1101 3.3 Install and configure storage devices (including RAID)

questions.questionText: Select the pin count for each memory module type.

dropdowns.prompt: Desktop DDR4 DIMM
Laptop DDR4 SO-DIMM
Desktop DDR3 DIMM

explanation.correct: Desktop DDR4 DIMMs have 288 pins, DDR4 SO-DIMMs have 260 pins, and desktop DDR3 DIMMs have 240 pins.
explanation.incorrect: Pin counts and notch positions differ so that incompatible modules cannot be installed.
explanation.examTip: DDR3 = 240, DDR4 = 288, DDR4 SO-DIMM = 260.

metadata.examObjective: 220-1101 3.2 Compare different types of RAM

questions.questionText: Select the component that each power connector feeds.

dropdowns.prompt: 24-pin ATX
PCIe 6+2 pin
4+4 pin EPS
SATA power

explanation.correct: The 24-pin powers the motherboard, PCIe power feeds GPUs, EPS feeds the CPU, and SATA power feeds drives.
explanation.incorrect: Each connector has a distinct shape and purpose.
explanation.examTip: Match connectors to components: 24-pin, EPS, PCIe, SATA.

metadata.examObjective: 220-1101 3.5 Install the appropriate power supply

questions.questionText: Select the expansion card that matches each requirement.

dropdowns.prompt: Adds additional Ethernet ports
Records an HDMI video signal from a console
Provides multichannel analog audio outputs

explanation.correct: A NIC adds network ports, a capture card records video input, and a sound card provides audio outputs.
explanation.incorrect: The other cards do not provide those functions.
explanation.examTip: Know the purpose of each add-on card.

metadata.examObjective: 220-1101 3.4 Install and configure motherboards, CPUs, and add-on cards

questions.questionText: Place the laser printing process steps in the correct order.

explanation.correct: The laser printing process is processing, charging, exposing, developing, transferring, fusing, and cleaning.
explanation.incorrect: Fusing occurs after the toner is transferred to the paper, and cleaning happens last.
explanation.examTip: Process, Charge, Expose, Develop, Transfer, Fuse, Clean.

metadata.examObjective: 220-1101 3.6 Deploy and configure multifunction devices/printers

questions.questionText: Place the steps for installing a CPU and cooler in the correct order.

orderItems.text: Lower and lock the retention arm
Power off, unplug, and ground yourself with an ESD strap
Align the notches or triangle and seat the CPU in the socket
Apply thermal paste and mount the heatsink and fan

explanation.correct: Safety and ESD precautions come first, then the CPU is seated and locked, followed by thermal paste and the cooler.
explanation.incorrect: Thermal paste and the cooler go on only after the CPU is secured.
explanation.examTip: Always apply ESD precautions before handling components.

metadata.examObjective: 220-1101 3.4 Install and configure motherboards, CPUs, and add-on cards

questions.questionText: Which cloud service model provides virtual machines, storage, and networking while the customer manages the operating system?

explanation.correct: Infrastructure as a Service provides virtualized compute, storage, and network resources, and the customer manages the OS and applications.
explanation.incorrect: PaaS manages the OS and runtime, SaaS delivers complete applications, and DaaS delivers desktops.
explanation.examTip: You manage the OS = IaaS.

metadata.examObjective: 220-1101 4.1 Summarize cloud computing concepts

questions.questionText: A developer wants to deploy code without managing servers or operating systems. Which cloud service model fits?

explanation.correct: Platform as a Service provides a managed runtime where developers deploy code without managing the underlying servers or OS.
explanation.incorrect: IaaS requires managing the OS, SaaS delivers finished applications, and on-premises hosting is not cloud.
explanation.examTip: Deploy code only = PaaS.

metadata.examObjective: 220-1101 4.1 Summarize cloud computing concepts

questions.questionText: Which hypervisor type runs directly on the physical hardware without a host operating system?

options.text: A container engine such as Docker

explanation.correct: Type 1 hypervisors run directly on hardware and are common in data centers.
explanation.incorrect: Type 2 hypervisors run on top of a host OS, and container engines share the host kernel rather than being hypervisors.
explanation.examTip: Type 1 = bare-metal; Type 2 = hosted.

metadata.examObjective: 220-1101 4.2 Summarize aspects of client-side virtualization

questions.scenarioText: A company must keep regulated customer data in a data center it controls but wants to use a provider's elastic compute resources for its public web front end.
questions.questionText: Which cloud deployment model BEST fits this requirement?

explanation.correct: A hybrid cloud combines private infrastructure with public cloud resources, allowing sensitive data to stay on-premises while using elastic public capacity.
explanation.incorrect: A purely public cloud would not keep the regulated data in the company's own data center, and a purely private cloud lacks elastic public capacity.
explanation.examTip: Mix of on-prem/private and public = hybrid.

metadata.examObjective: 220-1101 4.1 Summarize cloud computing concepts

questions.scenarioText: Several hospitals jointly fund a cloud environment that meets their shared regulatory requirements. It is not available to the general public.
questions.questionText: Which cloud deployment model is described?

options.text: Private cloud for a single hospital

explanation.correct: A community cloud is shared by organizations with common requirements such as compliance and is not open to the general public.
explanation.incorrect: Public clouds are open to anyone, hybrid clouds mix models, and a single-hospital private cloud serves only one organization.
explanation.examTip: Shared by several organizations with similar needs = community.

metadata.examObjective: 220-1101 4.1 Summarize cloud computing concepts

questions.questionText: Answer Yes if the statement is true, or No if it is false.

statements.text: Microsoft 365 is an example of SaaS.
In SaaS, the customer is responsible for patching the underlying operating system.
Metered service means customers pay based on resources used.
A private cloud must always be hosted by a third-party provider.

explanation.correct: SaaS delivers complete applications, the provider handles the underlying OS, metered services are billed by usage, and private clouds can be hosted on-premises.
explanation.incorrect: Private clouds may be on-premises or hosted by a provider.
explanation.examTip: SaaS = software you consume, not infrastructure you manage.

metadata.examObjective: 220-1101 4.1 Summarize cloud computing concepts

questions.questionText: Answer Yes if the statement is true, or No if it is false.

statements.text: Containers share the host operating system kernel.
Each container requires its own full guest operating system.
Docker images are used to create containers.
Running Docker containers on Linux requires a hypervisor.

explanation.correct: Containers share the host kernel and are launched from images, which makes them lighter than VMs.
explanation.incorrect: Full guest OSes are a feature of VMs, and Linux containers use host kernel features rather than a hypervisor.
explanation.examTip: VMs virtualize hardware; containers virtualize the OS.

metadata.examObjective: 220-1101 4.2 Summarize aspects of client-side virtualization

questions.questionText: Select ALL hypervisors that are commonly classified as Type 1.

explanation.correct: ESXi, Xen-based hypervisors, and Hyper-V run directly on hardware (Hyper-V runs as a layer beneath the management OS).
explanation.incorrect: VirtualBox and VMware Workstation are hosted Type 2 hypervisors.
explanation.examTip: Workstation and VirtualBox = Type 2.

metadata.examObjective: 220-1101 4.2 Summarize aspects of client-side virtualization

questions.questionText: Select the cloud concept that matches each description.

dropdowns.prompt: Provider hosts VMs and customer manages the OS
Provider hosts a runtime and customer deploys code
Provider delivers a complete application over the internet
Infrastructure shared by organizations with common requirements

explanation.correct: IaaS delivers infrastructure, PaaS delivers a platform, SaaS delivers applications, and community clouds are shared by organizations with common needs.
explanation.incorrect: The other models differ by who manages which layer or who may use the cloud.
explanation.examTip: Responsibility shifts to the provider from IaaS to PaaS to SaaS.

metadata.examObjective: 220-1101 4.1 Summarize cloud computing concepts

questions.questionText: Drag each service into the cloud service model it represents.

explanation.correct: EC2 and Azure VMs provide infrastructure, App Service and App Engine are platforms, and Salesforce and Microsoft 365 are finished applications.
explanation.incorrect: Platforms provide a runtime, whereas finished applications are SaaS.
explanation.examTip: IaaS = VMs; PaaS = app platforms; SaaS = finished apps.

metadata.examObjective: 220-1101 4.1 Summarize cloud computing concepts

questions.questionText: Place the steps for creating a new virtual machine on a Type 1 hypervisor in order.

orderItems.text: Install the guest OS and guest tools
Create the VM and assign vCPU, vRAM, virtual disk, and vNIC

explanation.correct: Virtualization must be enabled, the hypervisor installed, the VM defined with virtual hardware, media attached, and then the guest OS installed.
explanation.incorrect: The guest OS cannot be installed before the VM and its virtual hardware exist.
explanation.examTip: Check BIOS/UEFI virtualization support first.

metadata.examObjective: 220-1101 4.2 Summarize aspects of client-side virtualization

questions.questionText: Which command scans and repairs corrupted protected Windows system files?

explanation.correct: System File Checker (sfc /scannow) verifies protected system files and replaces corrupted ones from a cached copy.
explanation.incorrect: chkdsk checks the file system and disk, gpupdate refreshes Group Policy, and diskpart manages disks and partitions.
explanation.examTip: System files = sfc; disk errors = chkdsk.

metadata.examObjective: 220-1102 1.2 Use the appropriate Microsoft command-line tool

questions.questionText: Which command checks a disk for file system errors and attempts to locate bad sectors and recover readable data?

explanation.correct: chkdsk /r locates bad sectors and recovers readable information, and it implies /f.
explanation.incorrect: sfc checks system files, format erases a volume, and gpresult reports Group Policy results.
explanation.examTip: chkdsk /f fixes errors; /r also scans for bad sectors.

metadata.examObjective: 220-1102 1.2 Use the appropriate Microsoft command-line tool

questions.questionText: A new drive is installed but does not appear in File Explorer. Which tool should the technician use to initialize it and create a volume?

explanation.correct: Disk Management initializes disks, creates partitions and volumes, and assigns drive letters.
explanation.incorrect: Device Manager manages drivers, Services manages services, and Event Viewer shows logs.
explanation.examTip: New disk needs initialize + format = Disk Management.

metadata.examObjective: 220-1102 1.3 Use features and tools of the Microsoft Windows OS

questions.scenarioText: A technician has been told to manually edit a registry value to troubleshoot an application problem.
questions.questionText: What should the technician do FIRST?

options.text: Disable UAC and edit the registry offline
Export a backup of the relevant registry keys (or create a restore point)
Delete the key before editing it

explanation.correct: The registry is critical, so a backup or restore point must be created before any manual edits so changes can be reversed.
explanation.incorrect: sfc does not protect the registry, disabling UAC is unrelated and lowers security, and deleting the key first removes the original state.
explanation.examTip: Back up before regedit changes.

metadata.examObjective: 220-1102 1.3 Use features and tools of the Microsoft Windows OS

questions.scenarioText: A technician must repurpose a USB drive that still shows old partitions and must remove all partition data from it using diskpart.
questions.questionText: After selecting the disk in diskpart, which command removes all partition and volume information?

explanation.correct: The clean command erases the partition table information on the selected disk.
explanation.incorrect: format creates a file system on a volume, convert changes the partition style (and requires an empty disk), and list volume only displays information.
explanation.examTip: diskpart: select disk, clean, then create partition.

metadata.examObjective: 220-1102 1.2 Use the appropriate Microsoft command-line tool

questions.questionText: Which Linux command displays the current working directory?

explanation.correct: pwd prints the full path of the current working directory.
explanation.incorrect: ls lists files, cd changes directory, and grep searches text.
explanation.examTip: pwd = print working directory.

metadata.examObjective: 220-1102 1.11 Identify common features and tools of the Linux client/desktop OS

questions.questionText: What do the permissions set by chmod 755 file.sh grant?

options.text: Owner: read-only; group and others: read/execute
Owner: read/write/execute; group and others: read/execute
Owner: read/execute; group and others: read/write/execute

explanation.correct: 755 means owner rwx (7), group r-x (5), and others r-x (5).
explanation.incorrect: The other options do not match the numeric values: 7 = rwx, 5 = r-x.
explanation.examTip: 4 = read, 2 = write, 1 = execute.

metadata.examObjective: 220-1102 1.11 Identify common features and tools of the Linux client/desktop OS

questions.scenarioText: A Linux administrator must find all lines containing the word 'failed' (case-insensitive) in /var/log/auth.log, which requires elevated privileges.
questions.questionText: Which command should the administrator run?

explanation.correct: sudo provides elevated rights and grep -i performs a case-insensitive search for the text 'failed' in the file.
explanation.incorrect: grep -v inverts the match, ls lists files, and chmod changes permissions.
explanation.examTip: grep searches text; sudo elevates.

metadata.examObjective: 220-1102 1.11 Identify common features and tools of the Linux client/desktop OS

questions.scenarioText: A server takes a full backup every Sunday night and a differential backup each weeknight. Its drive fails on Thursday afternoon.
questions.questionText: Which backups are required to restore the server?

options.text: The Sunday full backup plus the Wednesday night differential backup
The Wednesday night differential backup only
The Sunday full backup plus the Monday, Tuesday, and Wednesday differential backups

explanation.correct: A differential backup contains all changes since the last full backup, so only the full backup and the most recent differential are needed.
explanation.incorrect: Using only the full backup loses weekday changes, you do not need every differential, and a differential alone lacks the base data.
explanation.examTip: Differential = full + latest differential; incremental = full + all incrementals.

metadata.examObjective: 220-1102 4.3 Implement workstation backup and recovery methods

questions.questionText: Which Windows feature provides full-disk encryption?

explanation.correct: BitLocker encrypts entire volumes to protect data if a device is lost or stolen.
explanation.incorrect: The firewall filters traffic, Disk Cleanup removes temporary files, and System Restore reverts system settings.
explanation.examTip: BitLocker = Windows; FileVault = macOS.

metadata.examObjective: 220-1102 2.5 Manage and configure basic security settings in the Microsoft Windows OS

questions.scenarioText: After installing an unsigned utility, a Windows PC became unstable. The user wants to revert system files and settings to an earlier time but keep all personal documents.
questions.questionText: Which tool should the technician use to revert the system to a previous state while keeping personal documents?

options.text: Reset this PC with Remove everything

explanation.correct: System Restore reverts system files, drivers, and settings to an earlier restore point without removing personal files.
explanation.incorrect: Resetting with Remove everything erases data, Disk Cleanup removes temporary files, and defragmenting does not undo changes.
explanation.examTip: System Restore does not restore deleted personal documents.

metadata.examObjective: 220-1102 1.3 Use features and tools of the Microsoft Windows OS

questions.scenarioText: A shared folder has the share permission Full Control for Everyone and the NTFS permission Read for the Sales group. A Sales user connects over the network and tries to edit a file.
questions.questionText: What level of access will the user have to the file?

explanation.correct: When share and NTFS permissions both apply, the most restrictive effective permission wins, which is Read.
explanation.incorrect: Full Control and Modify exceed the NTFS Read permission, and access is not denied because both permission sets allow at least read.
explanation.examTip: Network access = most restrictive of share and NTFS.

metadata.examObjective: 220-1102 2.5 Manage and configure basic security settings in the Microsoft Windows OS

questions.scenarioText: A PC is running slowly. Task Manager shows 100 percent disk usage, but the technician needs to see which specific files and processes are causing the disk activity.
questions.questionText: Which tool provides per-process disk activity and the files being accessed?

explanation.correct: Resource Monitor (resmon) shows detailed CPU, memory, disk, and network usage, including disk activity by process and file.
explanation.incorrect: Disk Cleanup removes files, msconfig manages boot and startup, and Windows Security provides malware protection.
explanation.examTip: Detailed live per-process I/O = Resource Monitor.

metadata.examObjective: 220-1102 1.3 Use features and tools of the Microsoft Windows OS

questions.questionText: Select ALL macOS features or utilities.

explanation.correct: Time Machine (backup), Spotlight (search), Mission Control (windows and desktops), and Disk Utility (disks) are macOS tools.
explanation.incorrect: Event Viewer is a Windows log viewer.

metadata.examObjective: 220-1102 1.10 Identify common features and tools of the macOS/desktop OS

questions.questionText: Select ALL valid Linux commands.

explanation.correct: ls, pwd, and grep are Linux commands.

explanation.examTip: Linux uses ifconfig/ip; Windows uses ipconfig.

metadata.examObjective: 220-1102 1.11 Identify common features and tools of the Linux client/desktop OS

questions.questionText: Select ALL Windows tools that help investigate recent system errors and performance.

explanation.correct: Event Viewer shows logs, and Performance Monitor and Resource Monitor show resource usage.
explanation.incorrect: Disk Cleanup and Optimize Drives are maintenance utilities, not diagnostic monitors.
explanation.examTip: Logs = Event Viewer; metrics = Performance/Resource Monitor.

metadata.examObjective: 220-1102 1.3 Use features and tools of the Microsoft Windows OS

questions.questionText: Select ALL features available in Windows Pro but NOT in Windows Home.

explanation.correct: Pro adds BitLocker, Group Policy editing, Remote Desktop hosting, and domain join.

metadata.examObjective: 220-1102 1.1 Identify basic features of Microsoft Windows editions

questions.questionText: Answer Yes if the statement is true, or No if it is false.

statements.text: msconfig can be used to configure Safe Boot.
System Restore can bring back deleted personal documents.
Task Manager can end an unresponsive process.
Disk Cleanup defragments a hard drive.

explanation.correct: msconfig configures boot options, Task Manager ends processes, and System Restore does not restore personal documents. Disk Cleanup deletes unneeded files.
explanation.incorrect: Defragmenting is done by Optimize Drives.
explanation.examTip: Know what each utility does and does not do.

metadata.examObjective: 220-1102 1.3 Use features and tools of the Microsoft Windows OS

questions.questionText: Answer Yes if the statement is true, or No if it is false.

statements.text: sudo runs a command with elevated privileges.
chmod changes file ownership.
chown changes the owner of a file.
pwd lists files in the current directory.

explanation.correct: sudo elevates, chown changes the owner, chmod changes permissions, and pwd prints the working directory.
explanation.incorrect: ls lists files, and chmod does not change ownership.
explanation.examTip: chmod = permissions; chown = owner.

metadata.examObjective: 220-1102 1.11 Identify common features and tools of the Linux client/desktop OS

questions.questionText: Answer Yes if the statement is true, or No if it is false.

statements.text: An incremental backup copies data changed since the last backup of any type.
A differential backup copies data changed since the last full backup.
Restoring from incrementals requires the last full backup and all later incrementals.
A differential backup clears the archive bit.

explanation.correct: Incrementals depend on a chain from the last full backup, differentials depend on the last full plus the latest differential, and differentials do not clear the archive bit.
explanation.incorrect: Incremental backups clear the archive bit; differential backups do not.
explanation.examTip: Full and incremental clear the archive bit; differential does not.

metadata.examObjective: 220-1102 4.3 Implement workstation backup and recovery methods

questions.questionText: Answer Yes if the statement is true, or No if it is false.

statements.text: Ctrl+Shift+Esc opens Task Manager.
Windows+R opens the Run dialog.

Windows+L signs the user out and closes all applications.

metadata.examObjective: 220-1102 1.3 Use features and tools of the Microsoft Windows OS

questions.questionText: Answer Yes if the statement is true, or No if it is false.

statements.text: Windows Security provides real-time malware protection.
UAC prompts for elevation when administrative rights are needed.
Standard users can install system-wide software without any credentials.

questions.questionText: Select the command that performs each task.

Force a refresh of Group Policy settings
Create a new file system on a volume

questions.questionText: Select the Windows console that manages each item.

Scheduled tasks
Disk partitions and volumes

metadata.examObjective: 220-1102 1.3 Use features and tools of the Microsoft Windows OS

questions.questionText: Select the command-line tool that matches each task.

Restart the computer immediately
Display the Windows version in a dialog
Show the currently logged-on user name

metadata.examObjective: 220-1102 1.2 Use the appropriate Microsoft command-line tool

questions.questionText: Select the Windows utility that best fits each task.

Delete temporary files to free up space
Reduce fragmentation on a mechanical hard drive
View real-time per-process disk, network, and memory usage

explanation.incorrect: Each utility has one primary function.

metadata.examObjective: 220-1102 1.3 Use features and tools of the Microsoft Windows OS

questions.questionText: Place the Windows boot process steps in the correct order.

questions.questionText: Place the CompTIA troubleshooting methodology steps in the correct order.

questions.questionText: Drag each tool or command to the operating system it belongs to.
